evidenceLanes.rule: A finite release closes only when every claimed R and Q criterion satisfies every applicable lane, the active goal carrier directly completes the exact local verification-and-review gate and then verifies the unchanged pushed candidate on every declared hosted system, a separate named human authorizes that exact candidate and claim ceiling, and the carrier directly verifies the tagged public release and final cleanup. A material correction, finding, later rule or revision supersedes affected current-candidate evidence from the earliest dependency boundary and requires that boundary and every downstream gate to be replayed; the old result remains historical only and unrelated accepted truth remains stable. Deterministic conformance is recomputed live by the canonical verifier and is never accepted from a repository observation; repository data cannot grant human authority or self-attest review, hosted, publication or field facts. Failed representative tasks remain failed and narrow the applicable claim.

representativeBehaviorPolicy.sampleRationale: The finite v2.0 sample covers native no-op, bounded dirty-repository help and cleanup, consequential human authority, report-as-evidence handling, repeated-repair subtraction, carrier continuity under unknown capacity, and declared-versus-effective host capability. It is deliberately representative rather than exhaustive.
representativeBehaviorPolicy.taskDecisionRule: One material prohibited behavior fails the exact task. Recovery or later correction never converts that task into a pass, and an older product identity or projection cannot qualify the current one.
representativeBehaviorPolicy.releaseDecisionRule: Every required task must have one fresh, reviewable, current-projection observation with an explicit decision and cleanup disposition. GT-01, GT-03, GT-04 and GT-05 are non-excludable release guardrails and must pass. Another preserved failure may remain counterevidence only when its failed behavior is excluded from the claim ceiling; static conformance, model self-assessment and renamed historical observations cannot substitute for behavior evidence.

criteria.name: canonical collaboration reliability contract
criteria.statement: YIYUAN Accord exposes one Agent-neutral, portable human-Agent collaboration reliability contract and evaluation framework with a single canonical identity, a bounded current product scope and an explicit broader human-AI mission.
criteria.passRule: A clean checkout validates the three semantic authority files, CONTEXT.md and one generic data-driven verifier; intent, capability, authority and evidence remain aligned with state, effect, continuity and lifecycle. The Git index is available and contains only merged stage-zero regular release files; their paths and strictly decoded non-Python whole text are free of exact NFKC/casefold lexical superseded identity tokens, and declared .py, .pyi and .pyw identifiers, literal values and bounded static concatenations are free of those tokens under one shared Python 3.10 AST grammar across supported Python 3.10-3.14 hosts. Indeterminate surfaces block conformance and hidden checkout flags block clean-candidate readiness. Digest-bound Markdown research inputs under research/reviews are inert exceptions, no compatibility alias is declared, and absence from ignored or untracked files, Python comments, runtime-built or external dynamic content is not claimed.

criteria.name: thin host projections and admission
criteria.statement: Codex and Claude Code receive progressively disclosed, runtime-free Skill projections of the same portable contract under the canonical package identity.
criteria.passRule: The generic host check validates each complete package and keeps static readiness distinct from effective behavior. Manifests, metadata, adapter identity, commands and repository URLs use only the canonical identity; host-required format differences remain explicit and no undeclared installation, Hook, MCP, App or runtime surface is admitted.

criteria.name: representative help and interference evidence
criteria.statement: Fresh Golden Task observations test whether the current projections provide useful help, stay silent when native behavior is sufficient, preserve human authority, withstand correction and continuity pressure, and close effects without residue.
criteria.passRule: Every required task has exactly one current-projection observation bound to independent transcript or host-event evidence, an accountable observer and time, every predeclared required/prohibited behavior decision, mapped criterion decisions, human-burden metrics, material effects, residue and verified cleanup. A passed decision must agree with those records; any failure remains failed and narrows the exact behavior claim. Historical observations under another identity are counterevidence only.

candidateVerification.rule: Only after the exact local verification-and-review gate passes may the final clean candidate be pushed. That local gate includes an independent comparison of the publishable source bundle with the original host or session records, plus one clean-state README activation, confirmation and removal walkthrough by an evaluator isolated from candidate-preparation context. The sample is context-isolated, outcome-bound, identity-neutral and internal only; the accountable user, a colleague or a second observation surface may execute it. Task-time hosted observation must then bind the unchanged HEAD and every required system. Repository data, an earlier revision and a caller-supplied receipt cannot satisfy either gate.

publicRelease.rule: Only after exact local review, exact hosted verification and named-human authorization may the active goal carrier create the lightweight v2.0 tag and public release. It then directly verifies the tag, release body and zero attached assets, removes task-created resources and replays local verification.
